title: Pop Culture Digest — Saturday, November 14, 2026
description:
Saturday · November 14, 2026
Pop Culture Digest
What’s actually dominating today
U2’s first album in nine years closes with Dolly Parton’s final recording, Taylor Swift is set to return to the CMA Awards stage for the first time in 13 years, Johnny Depp’s Ebenezer takes No. 1 at the Friday box office, and the Dune: Part Three cast pranks Rylan Clark for Children in Need.
Music

Dolly Parton’s final recording, “Torn,” closes U2’s new album Carnaval de Luz

U2 released Carnaval de Luz on Friday. It’s their 16th studio album and their first full album of new material in nine years. The final track, “Torn,” is a duet between Bono and Dolly Parton, who recorded her vocal in June, before she died in August at 80. Parton wrote the song as a story about a woman choosing between two men. Bono and Snow Patrol’s Johnny McDaid rewrote it as a song about a mother watching her family split apart. “When she got ill, she got out of her bed to sing this song,” Bono told Rolling Stone. Producer Jacknife Lee says Parton approved the final mix and “loved it.”

USA Today calls the album “glorious” and “unpredictable.” It also features “The Mirror Maker (Rosalía),” a song inspired by the Latin Grammys winner. Brian Eno co-wrote and plays synth on three songs, Martin Garrix co-wrote “Glorify,” and Daniel Lanois plays pedal steel. But USA Today says “Torn” is the song grabbing the headlines.

Listen on Spotify →   ·   Rolling Stone →   ·   USA Today review →

Music

Taylor Swift will perform at the CMA Awards for the first time in 13 years

The Country Music Association and ABC announced Friday that Swift will perform at the 60th CMA Awards this Wednesday, Nov. 18, in Nashville. Her last performance on the show was in 2013, when she received the Pinnacle Award and sang “Red” with Vince Gill and Alison Krauss. She’s nominated for Single of the Year for “I Knew It, I Knew You,” the song she wrote for Toy Story 5. It’s her 26th career CMA nomination. Billboard says the song spent two weeks at No. 1 on the Hot 100, and People reports it was her first song to top U.S. country radio in 13 years.

Organizers haven’t said what she’ll sing, though Variety expects her to perform the nominated song. Lainey Wilson hosts for a third straight year, and Ella Langley leads the nominations with nine. Luke Combs, Chris Stapleton, Kacey Musgraves and Mumford & Sons are also on the lineup, along with a planned tribute to Dolly Parton. The show airs live on ABC and Disney+ at 8 p.m. ET and streams on Hulu the next day.

Listen on Spotify →   ·   Variety →   ·   Billboard →   ·   CMA Awards announcement →

Movies

Johnny Depp’s Ebenezer takes No. 1 at the Friday box office, and Godzilla Minus Zero drops hard

Ti West’s gothic A Christmas Carol made $7.1 million on Friday, including $1.5 million from Thursday previews. Deadline says it’s headed for a $20 million-plus domestic opening, close to where Depp’s Black Mass ($22.6 million) and Public Enemies ($25.2 million) started. MovieWeb notes it’s Depp’s first No. 1 movie since Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald in 2018. Critics are mixed, with 53% on Rotten Tomatoes, but audiences gave it 4.5 stars in PostTrak exit polls. The film cost a net $38 million.

Godzilla Minus Zero set a record last weekend for the biggest North American opening by a live-action foreign-language film. This weekend it’s on pace to fall about 74%, to around $8 million, which puts it third behind The Cat in the Hat. David Leitch’s How to Rob a Bank, with Nicholas Hoult and Zoë Kravitz, is tracking for about a $4 million opening, against a reported net budget of $40 million.

Ebenezer official trailer on YouTube →   ·   Deadline →

Movies

The Dune: Part Three cast prank Rylan Clark for Children in Need, and the clip is everywhere

BBC presenter Rylan Clark thought he was doing a normal Dune: Part Three junket interview with Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya, Jason Momoa and Anya Taylor-Joy. In fact, three children were feeding the stars instructions through earpieces. They had Taylor-Joy stop the interview to meditate and lead an “ohm” chant, and they had Chalamet announce he was bidding on an air fryer, then lose the bid. They also had him stroke Clark’s beard. “Is this? Can I?” he asked, while Zendaya added, “It looks so smooth and shiny.”

The full prank aired during Friday night’s BBC Children in Need appeal, which the BBC says raised £38.7 million by the end of the live show. It comes as the Dune: Part Three press tour gets going. Denis Villeneuve’s trilogy finale opens Dec. 18, the same day as Avengers: Doomsday.

Dune: Part Three official trailer on YouTube →   ·   The prank (BBC Children in Need) on YouTube →   ·   TheWrap →   ·   BBC →

Bottom of the news

  • BTS won Album of the Year, the top prize, at the 2026 Melon Music Awards for Arirang, but didn’t attend the ceremony.
  • Avril Lavigne announced the birth of her first child, a daughter, on Instagram.
  • Amazon MGM released the trailer for Michael B. Jordan’s The Thomas Crown Affair, which he directs and stars in with Adria Arjona; it opens March 5, 2027.
  • Daniel Kaluuya and Tyriq Withers gave a viral airport interview in Eugene, Oregon, after Friday’s nationwide FAA ground stop, with Withers riffing on the “Bella Noche” meme.
  • Fall Out Boy released “ACES,” their first new original single in more than three years, and announced the Twilight of the Punks stadium and arena tour for 2027.
  • P!nk announced a Las Vegas residency at Sphere, the first by a solo female artist there, starting Sept. 29.
  • Washington Commanders quarterback Sam Hartman will be the lead of The Bachelor season 30, premiering in March 2027.
  • Mariah Carey released an official video for her 2001 Glitter ballad “Never Too Far,” 25 years after the song came out.
  • Alex Warren hosts the Kids’ Choice Awards tonight on CBS and Nickelodeon.
